newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Packer's PBL still keen on S.African tv.
newsitem.headline: Packer's PBL still keen on S.African tv.

text.p: Kerry Packer's television and magazine group Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd (PBL) said on Tuesday it remained hopeful of winning the licence to establish a television station in South Africa.
"This is an investment that PBl takes very seriously," PBL business development manager James McLachlan told Reuters.

McLachlan said South African regulators were due to announce licence conditions such as content and advertising limits by the end of April or in early May, with up to six consortiums expected to apply for a licence in July to be followed by submissions and public hearings.
He said the successful applicant was likely to be announced in November this year, 17 months after the company revealed its interest in South Africa's first free-to-air television station.

PBL said in late April 1996 that it had formed the Station for the Nation consortium which included Johannesburg-based entertainment group Interleisure Ltd and Moribo Investments, which has links to the ruling African National Congress.
McLachlan said each partner would have a 20 percent stake in the station, with local black investors to be sought to invest in the other 40 percent.

"It (the station) may be floated down the track but that is not our intention in the early days," he said. The other major candidate for the licence is a group led by Quentin Green, the former chairman of the South African Broadcasting Corp.
PBL, the operator of the leading Nine television network in Australia, is controlled by billionaire businessman Kerry Packer.
